candidate.answerReason: The difference a − b is the weight of one-sixth of a bucket's capacity of water. Filling from two-thirds to full adds twice that amount, giving a + 2(a − b) = 3a − 2b.

methods.label: Compare equal amounts of water
methods.explanation:
The bucket itself has the same weight in both measurements, so the difference \(a-b\) comes entirely from the extra water. The difference in fill levels is
\[
\frac23-\frac12=\frac16.
\]
Thus \(\frac16\) of the bucket's capacity of water weighs \(a-b\) kilograms.

Starting from the two-thirds-full measurement, filling the bucket requires another \(\frac13\) of its capacity. This is twice \(\frac16\), so the added water weighs \(2(a-b)\) kilograms. The full bucket therefore weighs
\[
a+2(a-b)=\boxed{3a-2b}
\]
kilograms, choice E.
